subject: french
title: Stretch: School Rules, Uniform & Future Plans
welcome_lead: Stretch into school rules, uniforms, and what you'll do après le bac.
meta_desc: GCSE French stretch: school rules with 'il faut', uniforms, near future tense.
final_note: Top-tier French! That blend of modal verbs and futures is Grade 8/9.

walkthroughs.h2: Il faut, on doit, il est interdit
walkthroughs.body_html:
French school rules use modal phrases + infinitive:

  • il faut + infinitive = you must (Il faut respecter les profs).
  • on doit + infinitive = one must (On doit porter un uniforme).
  • il est interdit de + infinitive = it's forbidden to (Il est interdit de fumer).
  • on n'a pas le droit de + infinitive = we're not allowed to.

French schools usually don't have uniforms, so this is a good comparison topic: En France, on n'a pas d'uniforme, mais en Angleterre on doit porter un uniforme noir avec une cravate. Opinions: Je pense que l'uniforme est pratique parce qu'on n'a pas besoin de choisir ses vêtements le matin.

The near future uses aller + infinitive: Je vais aller au lycée, Je vais étudier l'histoire à l'université, Plus tard, je voudrais devenir médecin. Useful jobs: médecin, professeur, ingénieur, infirmier/infirmière, avocat(e). The conditional je voudrais + infinitive = I would like to.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is correct for 'You must respect the teachers'?
What does 'Je vais étudier l'histoire à l'université' mean?
options: I am studying history at university
I am going to study history at university
I would like to study history at university
